title: Escrow Post-Closer Specialist
description:
Prophet Title is seeking a detail-oriented and organized Escrow Post-Closer to join our growing title and escrow team in Plano, TX.

This position focuses on the final stages of the escrow process after a real estate transaction has closed, ensuring all post-closing documentation, title policies, recordings, and transaction files are accurately completed and finalized.

This is an excellent opportunity for an entry-level or early-career professional with 1–2 years of relevant post-closing, title, or escrow experience who is looking to grow within the title industry.

The ideal candidate will have experience with title policy typing and preparation, strong organizational skills, and the ability to manage multiple completed transaction files in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities

- Post-Closing File Management: Review completed real estate transactions to ensure all required documentation is accurate, complete, and properly organized for final processing.

- Title Policy Typing & Preparation: Prepare, type, review, and process final title insurance policies, including applicable endorsements, ensuring accuracy and compliance with company and underwriter requirements.

- Recording & Document Processing: Coordinate the recording of deeds, deeds of trust, and other required documents with the appropriate county offices. Track recording confirmations and address rejected or outstanding documents.

- Document Review: Verify that all closing documents have been properly executed, notarized, and included in the completed transaction file.

- File Reconciliation: Assist with reviewing final escrow statements, disbursement records, and outstanding balances to ensure completed files are accurate and ready for final archiving.

- Outstanding Items & Follow-Up: Identify and resolve missing documents, outstanding title requirements, recording discrepancies, or other post-closing issues.

- Communication: Work closely with Escrow Officers, Escrow Assistants, title underwriters, lenders, and other parties to obtain outstanding documents and finalize completed transactions.

- Record Keeping & Compliance: Maintain accurate and organized post-closing records in accordance with company policies, title underwriter guidelines, and applicable regulations.

- Customer Service: Provide professional and timely communication to internal teams and external partners regarding post-closing matters.

Qualifications

Required

- 1–2+ years of experience in escrow post-closing, title insurance, or a related role involving post-closing responsibilities.

- Experience with title policy typing, preparation, and processing.

- Basic understanding of residential real estate closing documents and post-closing procedures.

- Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and organizational skills.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to manage multiple transaction files and meet deadlines.

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and general computer applications.

- Ability to work independently and collaborate with a team.

Preferred

- Experience with escrow and title software such as SoftPro, RamQuest, or similar platforms.

- Familiarity with Simplifile or other electronic recording systems.

- Knowledge of Texas title insurance policies, endorsements, and recording requirements.

- Experience working in a title company or escrow office.

- Familiarity with residential investment properties and wholesale real estate transactions.

- Experience processing a high volume of completed escrow files.

Work Environment

- In-office position: Must be local to the Plano, TX area.

- Collaborative, high-performance team environment.

- Fast-paced title and escrow operations supporting residential real estate transactions.

- Opportunities for professional development and career advancement.

Benefits

- Competitive salary on experience.

- Opportunities for career growth within the company.

- Supportive and collaborative work environment.

title: Investment Banking Associate, Restructuring
location: New York, NY; Red Bank, NJ
description:
Position: Restructuring Associate, Investment Banking

Location: New York, NY or Red Bank, NJ

Company Description

B. Riley Securities provides a full suite of investment banking, corporate finance, advisory, research, and sales and trading services. Investment banking services include initial, secondary and follow-on offerings, institutional private placements, merger and acquisition (M&A) advisory, SPACs, corporate restructuring and recapitalization. B. Riley is nationally recognized and highly ranked for its proprietary small-cap equity research.

Position Overview

We are seeking a full-time Associate to join our Restructuring group in New York or Red Bank, NJ, reporting to the Head of Restructuring. The group advises companies, boards, creditors, sponsors and investors on in-court and out-of-court restructurings, recapitalizations, distressed M&A, rescue financings and strategic alternatives. The Associate will own analytical workstreams, manage analysts, and work directly with clients, creditor groups, counsel and other advisors from mandate through resolution. Our lean deal teams give Associates early, substantial responsibility, including leading models and materials, participating in negotiations, and presenting to management teams and boards. We welcome candidates from restructuring investment banking groups and from restructuring advisory and turnaround firms. The base salary range for this position is $ 160,000 to $180,000, and the position is eligible for quarterly bonuses.

Key Responsibilities

  • Build and manage complex financial models, including cash flow and liquidity budgets , recovery and waterfall analyses, debt capacity builds, and other detailed valuation models.
  • Analyze capital structures, credit agreements, indentures, covenants and stakeholder positions.
  • Evaluate strategic alternatives for debtors, creditors, sponsors and investors, including liability management, distressed M&A, 363 sales, DIP and rescue financings.
  • Coordinate due diligence and execution with clients, counsel, lenders, investors and other transaction advisors.
  • Prepare restructuring presentations, creditor and board materials, CIMs, teasers and other transaction documents.
  • Support court-related work, including first day and other declarations, valuation reports, liquidation and plan feasibility analyses supporting disclosure statements, and expert testimony preparation.
  • Communicate deal dynamics clearly to clients and deal team members, including senior bankers and management to keep relevant parties informed of timelines and priorities.
  • Staff, review and train analysts, and ensure zero-defect work product across the team.
  • Support pitches and new business development, and partner with other B. Riley businesses on client solutions.
  • Participate in recruiting, training and mentoring.

Qualifications

  • 2 to 5 years of experience in a restructuring, special situations or liability management investment banking group, or at a restructuring advisory or turnaround consulting firm.
  • Direct experience with in-court and/or out-of-court restructurings, distressed M&A, recapitalizations or liability management transactions.
  • Familiarity with the Chapter 11 process and case reporting (e.g., MORs, SOFAs, DIP budgets and budget-to-actual reporting) a plus.
  • Advanced financial modeling and valuation skills, with fluency in credit documents, capital structures and recovery analysis.
  • Experience supervising and reviewing junior work.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to multitask, prioritize and perform under pressure in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.
  • Bachelor's degree required; MBA or CFA a plus.
  • FINRA SIE, Series 79 and Series 63 a plus but not required.

Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment: B. Riley Securities is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusion. We are pleased to consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, protected veterans status, Aboriginal/Native American status or any other legally-protected factors.
